title: Unified throttle + prefetch helpers for embeddings & rerank SDKs with streaming ergonomics
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build language-idiomatic helpers and example patterns across Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs to achieve API parity for embeddings and reranking endpoints. Focus areas: a) ergonomic paginated iterators that support batching, prefetch, and transparent retries; b) streaming generator patterns with clear cancellation/backpressure semantics; c) shared policy primitives (retry/backoff, token pagination naming, batch shaping) that can be implemented idiomatically in each language. Output must include runnable examples, tests, and a single cross-SDK design doc linked in links.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Each SDK exposes a paginated iterator/stream for embeddings and rerank that supports: page_size, batch_size, prefetch (1..4), and max_retries; 2) Examples for sync & async Python, TS (Promise/AsyncIterator), and Go (context + channel) that demonstrate cancellation and graceful shutdown; 3) SDKs surface standardized pagination_token name 'rw_pagination_token' and return consistent metadata keys: total_items, next_token, page_size; 4) Unit + e2e tests for retry behavior with injected transient failures; 5) Developer docs and 1 cross-SDK sample app in repo/sample-sdks/emb-rerank-prefetch.
decisions: Use 'rw_pagination_token' as canonical query key to avoid vendor collisions
Implement prefetch as a tunable integer; default=1 to minimize memory while enabling overlap
Retry policy: idempotent on embeddings/rerank read-only endpoints; use exponential backoff with jitter, max_retries default=3
Expose both high-level convenience iterator and low-level paginated_client for advanced control
Streaming: in TS use AsyncGenerator with AbortSignal for cancellation; Python uses async iterator with contextlib.asynccontextmanager; Go uses context.Context and a results channel
